newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag sees 97 sales up, profit to stay high.
newsitem.headline: Viag sees 97 sales up, profit to stay high.

text.p: German diversified group VIAG AG said on Friday it was confident it would increase sales in 1997 and keep earnings high despite unavoidable start-up losses resulting from its drive into the telecommunications market.

In 1996, operating profit before tax rose to just under 2.4 billion marks from 2.1 billion marks according to provisional figures, Viag said in a statement. The company plans to keep its dividend for 1996 unchanged at 12 marks.
Sales rose to about 42.5 billion marks from 41.9 billion marks, Viag said.
The group said 1997 will see the implementation of projects to improve its portfolio and expand in telecommunications.
All divisions would continue with cost-cutting measures and efforts to improve their market position.
"As a result we are optimistic to continue to increase sales in the current year and to hold earnings at a high level despite unavoidable start-up losses in telecommunications," Viag said.
Viag's activities include power generation, the manufacture of packaging and chemicals, distribution and logistics, and telecommunications.
